metadata.description: Major hurricanes affecting Dade County during study period (1910-1930)
metadata.source: Built by Labor, Divided by Design research project; tracks from NOAA HURDAT2
metadata.note: For full official tracks, download NOAA HURDAT2 from https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/ — these are simplified representations of the approach and landfall.

properties.name: Great Miami Hurricane of 1926 - Landfall Point
properties.eye_passage: Eye passed directly over downtown Miami with ~35-minute lull
properties.affected_areas: Miami Beach, downtown waterfront, Coconut Grove, Hialeah, Moore Haven (Lake Okeechobee)
properties.significance: Effectively ended the Florida Land Boom of the 1920s. Occurred when many newcomers did not know hurricanes had a calm eye — many went outside during the lull and were killed by the back side of the storm.

properties.name: Great Miami Hurricane of 1926 - Track (simplified)
properties.notes: Simplified approach track from Atlantic through Miami and into Gulf of Mexico. Use NOAA HURDAT2 for full official track with 6-hour intervals.

properties.name: Okeechobee Hurricane of 1928 - Landfall Point
properties.affected_areas: Primary devastation at Lake Okeechobee; Palm Beach County landfall; Miami impact relatively minor
properties.significance: Killed ~2,500 mostly Black migrant farmworkers around Lake Okeechobee due to dike failure. Led to Hoover Dike construction. Miami felt effects but escaped major damage.
properties.miami_impact: Tropical-storm force winds; minor compared to 1926

properties.name: Okeechobee Hurricane of 1928 - Track (simplified)
properties.notes: Simplified approach track. Landfall at West Palm Beach then devastated Lake Okeechobee region. Use NOAA HURDAT2 for full official track.
